plants.name: Euphorbia pulcherrima
plants.description: Wild poinsettias grow into leggy shrubs and small trees. Their fiery crimson bracts look like petals and surround tiny yellow true flowers. The bracts glow in the short, bright days of winter in the mountains of southern Mexico, which is where the plant originated.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn through winter, peaking from December to February
plants.location: Southern Mexico and Central America, where it grows wild in seasonally dry forests; it is also grown worldwide as a holiday plant
plants.funFact: Poinsettias are short-day plants. They need long, uninterrupted nights to color up, which is why they peak around the winter solstice. The showy red parts are modified leaves, not petals.

plants.name: Delonix regia
plants.description: In the southern summer, this broad, umbrella-shaped tree turns into a canopy of scarlet-orange blossoms. Each flower has one petal streaked with white and gold. The feathery, fern-like leaves make a lacy backdrop for the blooms.
plants.bloomingSeason: Southern Hemisphere summer, roughly November to January
plants.location: Northern Australia, southern Africa and other tropical and subtropical regions of the Southern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: Native to Madagascar, the royal poinciana is endangered in the wild there. It is now planted in warm regions all over the world, so it is far more common in cultivation than in nature.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: In late spring, jacaranda trees fill the streets with clouds of lavender-blue trumpet flowers. When the blossoms fall, they leave a violet carpet on pavements and parked cars.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer in the Southern Hemisphere, around October to December
plants.location: Sydney and other parts of eastern Australia, South Africa and South America, where the tree is widely planted
plants.funFact: Jacaranda trees are native to South America but have become icons of cities such as Pretoria and Sydney. Local lore in Australia holds that a blossom falling on your head brings good luck.
